lessons.description: Grammar: the imperative of put. New language: bath, bathroom, bedroom, fridge, home, kitchen, living room, put, room, TV.
Grammar: There is… There are…; preposition next to. New language: hospital, park, shop.
Grammar: present simple; first person singular of live. New language: bird, flat, live (v), mouse, tree.
Grammar: present simple; first person singular of live; definite and indefinite article: the sea/a well. New language: fish, sea, smell, snail.
Grammar: imperatives: Cut! Stop!. New language: cold, cut, need, new, nice.
Grammar: imperative of verbs: wait, plant, grow, look at; possessive 's e.g. our children's children. New language: children, grow, hot, plant (v), seed, walk.
Grammar: determiner: lots of. New language: lots of, street.
Grammar: possessive adjective my; simple present of have got and live with I. New language: best, cow, field, nest, river.
Grammar: conjunction and; pronoun this. New language: brother, card, father, me, mother, sister.
Grammar: possessive 's: Dalia's family. New language: baby, family, grandfather, grandmother.
Grammar: numbers to 20; determiner any; question word which…?. New language: any, very, which.
Grammar: present simple, third person singular of verbs Be and have got; phrases with adjective + noun. New language: between, short, star, tall.
Grammar: imperatives Stand…, Stay (there). New language: preposition, stand, stay.
Grammar: present simple, first person plural (We) of verbs eat, go to bed, sleep, wake up; numbers 1-20. New language: chick, eat, now, sleep, wake up, we.
Grammar: subject pronouns I, you, he, she, we, they. New language: after, at, breakfast.
Grammar: prepositions in, with. New language: garden, people.
Grammar: can for ability; articles a, an, the, no article with plurals. New language: can, key, remember, sea, sweet (n).
Grammar: imperatives of common verbs (Sit, Go); imperatives with don't. New language: game, play, sit, down, write.
Grammar: can for ability; question How many?; numbers 1-20. New language: hop, read, run, skip, talk.
Grammar: question How many?; conjunction and. New language: make.
Grammar: possessive adjective our; pronouns this, that. New language: air, fly (v), fruit, sky.
Grammar: present simple, first person singular (I) with verb like + noun; conjunction and. New language: beach, ice cream, like, sand, tea.
Grammar: questions and sentences in the present simple with have got and can (see). New language: close (v), open (v), round (adv), wheel.
Grammar: imperatives of common verbs: affirmative and negative forms; object pronoun it. New language: catch, sentence, throw, water (v).
Grammar: adverbs here, there, today. New language: farm, goat, say, today.
Grammar: noun phrases: Nile fish, long tails; first person plural, present simple of verb + noun. New language: hippo, lay, metre, sharp, snake.
Grammar: can (for ability) + verb; nouns: singular and regular plurals. New language: camel, desert, elephant, forest, map, mountain.
Grammar: can (for ability); conjunction and. New language: alphabet, climb, jump, parrot, sing, swim, swing.
Grammar: can/can't (for ability); nouns: singular and regular plurals. New language: bat, but, lion.
Grammar: statements with have got and can + verb; noun phrases: short tails, wide feet. New language: about, drink (v), hump, order, water, wide.
Grammar: sentences in present simple with haven't, don't and can't + verb; common adjectives. New language: be, Bedouin, friend.
Grammar: can (for ability); prepositions in, up. New language: grass, phone, whale.
Grammar: there is/there are some with countable and uncountable nouns. New language: banana, bread, juice, milk, some, tomato.
Grammar: there is/there are some with countable and uncountable nouns. New language: carrot, peanut, potato, shelf, sugar.
Grammar: conjunction or. New language: or, orange, round (adj), think, vegetable.
Grammar: imperatives of common verbs and don't. New language: add, clean, glass, mango, mix, mixer, wash.
Grammar: can (for ability); possessive adjectives your, my. New language: favourite, food, good, smell (v), sweet (adj), taste (v).
Grammar: conjunction or; have got. New language: different, grape, onion, same.
Grammar: would like/'d like + noun; conjunctions: and, or. New language: I'd like…, would.
Grammar: is/is not; conjunction or; present simple like/don't like. New language: garlic, meat.
